brief_premise_checked.premise_as_given: "`liftPart` and `bathroomPod` appear ONLY in ALL_PLUGINS + ELEMENT_PLUGIN_IDS + STORE_ONLY_PLUGIN_IDS. They are documented compound MEMBERS and carry NO defineElement / L0 schema at all -- unlike their parent families."
brief_premise_checked.verdict_for_liftPart: SUBSTANTIALLY CONFIRMED, WITH ONE CORRECTION AND ONE ADDITION.
brief_premise_checked.correction: 'appear ONLY in [three registries]' is too narrow. liftPart also appears in the L0 Id BRAND union (Id.ts:108/188/239), in snapshotFamilyCoverage (:155), in ProjectSerializer (:1516/:1650 -- it is PERSISTED under key `liftParts`), in the lift undo adapter, and as a typed sub-array on the `lift.created` event payload (types.ts, `readonly parts: ReadonlyArray<{ readonly id: string; readonly kind: string; ...}>`). Five more registries than the premise names, and one of them is the persistence format.
brief_premise_checked.addition_the_premise_misses: The schema split is DELIBERATE AND WRITTEN DOWN, not an oversight -- and the doctrine is stated at Id.ts:113-127 for its sibling: the BRAND is promoted to L0 while the Zod SHAPE is not, 'because moving the schema changes what validates a persisted project, which is a C47 format question deserving its own blast radius'. Without the brand, `createId` -- the ONE id factory -- could not mint the id, 'leaving a caller with a hand-built string (a second vocabulary, C84 EI-8) or a cast'. Id.ts:102-104 says the LiftId promotion is 'THE PROMOTION liftReachableThroughComposedRuntime.test.ts ANTICIPATED'. So 'carries NO L0 schema' is true of the Zod shape and FALSE of the L0 type surface.
brief_premise_checked.parent_asymmetry_confirmed: The premise's 'unlike their parent families' holds: `lift` also has no defineElement (it is not in the 26-kind census either). The asymmetric pair is liftPart/lift vs water/pool -- `water` DOES have defineElement('water') at Water.ts:41 while `pool` has defineElement('pool') at Pool.ts:41. So the compound-member families are not uniformly schema-less; water is the counter-example.

smuggling_question.question: Brief s4 -- is this the 'MEMBER WITH NO CHANNEL, SMUGGLED onto another family's channel' pattern -- one element id appearing on two families?
smuggling_question.verdict: NO CHANNEL OF ITS OWN -- AND NOT SMUGGLED. The parts ride as a TYPED FIELD on the PARENT'S OWN event.
measurement: `grep -n 'liftPart' packages/runtime-composer/src/CommandEventBridge.ts` -> 6 hits, ALL inside `case 'lift.create':` (CEB:1560), NONE of them an emit of a `liftPart.*` event.
CEB:1788-1792 collects the committed parts into a local `_liftParts`, filtered by `part['parentId'] !== p.liftId`.

CEB:1795-1811 emits ONE `lift.created` carrying `parts: _liftParts as never` -- the parent's own typed event, whose payload type at packages/runtime-composer/src/types.ts:785 declares `readonly parts: ReadonlyArray<{ readonly id: string; readonly kind: string; ... }>`.
There is no `'liftPart.created'` key in the RuntimeEvents map: `grep -n "'liftPart" packages/runtime-composer/src/types.ts` -> no event key.
smuggling_question.why_it_is_not_smuggling: Smuggling would be ONE ID APPEARING ON TWO FAMILIES -- emitting a member under another family's event name so something draws it. I tested for exactly that and it does not happen. The `wall.created` events that DO fire inside `case 'lift.create':` (CEB:1671) iterate `_liftCommitted.get('wall')` and are skipped unless `wall['parentId'] === p.liftId`: they carry REAL `Wall` records with wall ids -- the shaft enclosure sides, which the code describes as 'a real `Wall` record the assembly already built ... so the §P2.1 mirror builds it exactly as it builds a hand-drawn wall'. No liftPart id is ever placed on a wall/slab/furniture event.
smuggling_question.the_refusal_is_explicit_elsewhere: The sibling case states the doctrine in the negative and names the contract: CommandEventBridge.ts:2028-2035, in `case 'pool.create':` -- "THE WATER IS NOT SMUGGLED THROUGH AS A SLAB ... Emitting `slab.created` for it to make something blue appear would put one id on two families and give the water a thickness it does not have -- C84 EI-9, and the same refusal the lift made when it declined to feed its compound into the massing store." That last clause is the lift's own recorded refusal.
smuggling_question.the_honest_state_named: liftPart HAS NO CHANNEL OF ITS OWN, and does not need one: it has no independent lifecycle to announce. Its create leg rides the parent event's `parts` field; its undo leg is `registerLiftRenderSink` (§LIFT94), because -- as bathroomPodMemberMirror.ts:29-31 records -- "there is no `'lift.deleted'` key in `RuntimeEvents`, so an undo could not be relayed as a bus event" and the lift had to hand-build a render sink to get what a store subscription gives for free.

findings.claim: The brief's 'appears ONLY in ALL_PLUGINS + ELEMENT_PLUGIN_IDS + STORE_ONLY_PLUGIN_IDS' undercounts by five registries, one of which is the PERSISTENCE FORMAT (ProjectSerializer key `liftParts`, snapshotFamilyCoverage :155). A family in the save format is not a registry-only id, and treating it as one is how a 'tidy up the orphan' action becomes a data-loss change.

findings.claim: Tested for the C84 EI-9 'one id on two families' pattern and it is ABSENT. liftPart records ride as the typed `parts` field on the parent's own `lift.created` event (CEB:1795-1811, types.ts:785), never re-emitted under another family's event name. The `wall.created` events fired inside `case 'lift.create':` carry real Wall records filtered by `parentId`, not cabin parts.

The lift compound is HALF-DRAWN IN PLAN and nothing declares it. Shaft walls are real Wall records and render in plan; the five cabin parts have no plan symbol. That reads to a user as a lift shaft with an empty car, not as a missing feature. Unlike the delete leg (declared in initTools §FT-WATER for water, and carried on mirror-debt.json for lift.delete), this asymmetry is written down nowhere.
